decisionTitle: test script uses `node --test` without an explicit `test/` path argument
rationale:
In this sandboxed execution environment, `node --test test/` (and even `node --test test` without trailing slash) fails with a spurious `Cannot find module '.../test'` MODULE_NOT_FOUND error from the CJS loader, even though the directory and file exist and are readable. Running bare `node --test` (Node's default recursive discovery of `**/*.test.js`) works correctly and picks up exactly `test/lib.test.js`, so `case-converter/package.json`'s `scripts.test` was set to `node --test` instead of `node --test test/`. This is functionally equivalent for this package (only one test directory exists) and `npm --prefix case-converter test` (the task's unitTestCmd) passes cleanly with it. Flagging this in case other utility packages in this repo hit the same directory-argument quirk in this environment.

Also followed FR-5/architecture.md over the task text where they diverged: `upper`/`lower` do a simple whole-string case change (not tokenize+rebuild), `title` only splits on whitespace (not on `_`/`-`/camelCase boundaries), while `camel`/`pascal`/`snake`/`kebab` use the full tokenizer (camelCase/PascalCase/snake_case/kebab-case/space/mixed separators/digit-run boundaries, Unicode-aware). Invalid mode throws a typed `CaseConverterError` (not `process.exit`), listing all valid modes in the message. `cli.js` was intentionally not created, per the task's explicit scope note.
